loci.name: extension-mechanism
loci.one_line: Which extension mechanism maximizes llm-d reuse for non-pod backends: file-discovery fed by an external generator (no Go), an out-of-tree EndpointDiscovery plugin in a thin downstream EPP build (exported registry, undocumented, no precedent), an in-tree fork (documented, merge burden), embedding llm-d scheduling/kv-cache packages in a custom router, or upstreaming the plugin — and what does each cost across llm-d's ~monthly release cadence?
loci.rationale: This is the strategy decision the user asked for. Code shows out-of-tree registration is technically sound (exported Registry + Register, importable runner) but the only documented path is editing runner.go, no downstream precedent exists, the interface is ~3 months old with Alpha/Beta lifecycle, and the docs' own plugin skeleton does not compile against HEAD. The investigator must commit to a ranked recommendation with a maintenance-cost argument, and settle whether library embedding is lightweight or heavyweight reuse.

loci.name: kv-event-path-off-k8s
loci.one_line: Does precise prefix-cache-aware routing (llm-d's flagship scorer) work when endpoints come from file/custom discovery — i.e. does the EPP-embedded KV indexer use Static Endpoint Mode (backends push to a bound ZMQ SUB) or a Kubernetes pod reconciler, and do KV-event identities (kv@ip:port@model) line up with EndpointDiscovery's NamespacedName ids?
loci.rationale: If precise prefix routing silently degrades off-k8s, the recommendation must say so and prescribe the approximate prefix scorer or a fix. The corpus documents both modes but never demonstrates precise routing with file discovery end-to-end; the no-k8s guide's plugin mix uses the approximate prefix-cache-scorer, which is itself a signal. Needs code-level reading of the precise-prefix plugin's indexer wiring in llm-d-router and llm-d-kv-cache.

loci.name: availability-and-lifecycle-off-k8s
loci.one_line: Outside Kubernetes the EPP becomes a fail-closed hard dependency and endpoint health/eviction becomes the caller's job — what is the production design for EPP HA (v0.9 multi-replica under file/custom discovery, replica consistency), health gating in lieu of pod readiness, and securing metrics scraping, ZMQ KV events and the ORIGINAL_DST header path?
loci.rationale: Fail-open vs fail-closed is a live maintainer dispute (agentgateway #1661 open); the corpus asserts but never shows that v0.9 HA replicas cover non-k8s discovery; security defaults are audited absences (plain-HTTP metrics, no ZMQ auth, TLS to EPP dropped when colocated). These determine the operational half of the roadmap.

loci.name: custom-discovery-plugin-design
loci.one_line: Since llm-d ships no dynamic discovery backend, what should a production custom EndpointDiscovery plugin (Consul/etcd/cloud SD/Slurm/Ray-fed) look like — watch vs poll, initial enumeration + Ready semantics, single-goroutine notifier ordering, health filtering, identity synthesis (NamespacedName, --pool-namespace), labels for P/D roles — using Dynamo (etcd/NATS), production-stack (StaticServiceDiscovery), RAMSES (Postgres-fed) and the file plugin as design references?
loci.rationale: Audited absence of any non-file plugin; the roadmap needs a concrete reference design and effort estimate. Converges rather than argues, so a moderate budget.

loci.name: topology-and-k8s-shims
loci.one_line: Which deployment topology fits which backend estate: router fully outside Kubernetes (file/custom discovery), router inside Kubernetes targeting out-of-cluster backends (file discovery via ConfigMap or custom plugin), or making backends real pods (Slinky slurm-operator) so stock InferencePool works — and are EndpointSlice/virtual-kubelet shims ever viable for the EPP?
loci.rationale: Corpus largely resolves the EndpointSlice/virtual-kubelet branch (InferencePool selects Pods only; interLink excludes long-running services; Slurm plugin egress-only) but leaves the hybrid and Slinky branches under-argued; the report's strategy table needs a topology decision rule.

loci.name: lost-k8s-policy-inputs
loci.one_line: What replaces the Kubernetes-only policy inputs off-cluster — InferenceObjective priority/SLO (FlowControl priority bands), InferenceModelRewrite (model aliasing, canary splits), PodMonitor metrics discovery — using static config, the Inference Payload Processor, or the gateway tier?
loci.rationale: Analyst A judged parity well covered; analyst B found an internal tension (platform-invariant claim vs listed inactive features). The gap is WHAT TO BUILD, which the corpus does not answer; a short pass suffices.
